title: Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in lib/http2.c via Malformed PUSH_PROMISE Headers
excerpt:
Summary
A heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in libcurl's HTTP/2 implementation. The on_header callback in lib/http2.c incorrectly treats header names and values provided by nghttp2 as null-terminated C-strings. Specifically, passing these pointers to curl_maprintf with the %s format specifier triggers an out-of-bounds read via strlen(), as nghttp2 provides raw byte buffers with explicit lengths, not null-terminated strings.
+1

Vulnerability Analysis & Root Cause
1. API Contract Violation: According to the nghttp2 documentation, the nghttp2_on_header_callback provides pointers to the header name and value (name, value) alongside their lengths (namelen, valuelen). The documentation explicitly states:

"The 'name' and 'value' pointers are NOT guaranteed to be null-terminated. [...] Applications MUST use the provided length parameters.".

2. Vulnerable Implementation: In lib/http2.c, the on_header function ignores the length parameters when formatting the string for PUSH_PROMISE headers, relying on curl_maprintf which internally uses strlen:

C

/* lib/http2.c around line 1642 - Vulnerable */
h = curl_maprintf("%s:%s", name, value); 
3. Execution Flow:

curl_maprintf parses the %s format specifier.

It internally calls strlen() on the name and value pointers.

Since the malicious server sends a header without a null byte, strlen() reads past the allocated buffer boundary until it hits a coincidental null byte in adjacent heap memory.

This results in an Out-of-Bounds Read.

Steps to Reproduce
1. Build Environment
Compile cURL with AddressSanitizer (ASAN) to visualize the memory violation:

Bash

./configure --with-nghttp2 --enable-debug CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -g" LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address"
make -j$(nproc)
2. Reproduction Script (http2_server.py)
This Python script (using h2) establishes an HTTP/2 connection and pushes a stream with a non-null-terminated header.

Python

    await writer.drain()

    data = await reader.read(65535)

summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in libcurl's HTTP/2 implementation when processing malformed PUSH_PROMISE headers due to misuse of curl_maprintf with non-null-terminated header names and values.

claims.text: curl_maprintf is called with %s format specifiers on header name and value pointers that are not null-terminated, causing strlen() to read past buffer boundaries
claims.reasoning: The code at lib/http2.c:1642 passes name and value pointers to curl_maprintf with %s format specifiers. Since nghttp2 does not guarantee null-termination (per external source), and curl_maprintf uses strlen for %s, this causes an out-of-bounds read when the buffers lack a terminating null byte.

on_header callback signature shows namelen and valuelen parameters are provided but ignored at line 1642

claims.text: on_header callback in lib/http2.c around line 1642
claims.reasoning: The deterministic checks confirm lib/http2.c exists and line 1642 contains the curl_maprintf call within the on_header function.

citations.note: The vulnerable curl_maprintf call is at line 1642 in the on_header function
on_header function definition starts at line 487

claims.text: sending a PUSH_PROMISE header with a name and value that lack null termination, provided by nghttp2 via its callback parameters namelen and valuelen
claims.reasoning: The on_header callback is registered for nghttp2 header events. When a PUSH_PROMISE frame arrives (frame type HEADERS with category NGHTTP2_HCAT_PUSH_PROMISE), the code at line 1642 processes the header name/value using %s without length limits.

citations.note: nghttp2_session_callbacks_set_on_header_callback(cbs, on_header) registers on_header as the header callback
on_header receives name, namelen, value, valuelen from nghttp2
Code context shows this is in the PUSH_PROMISE handling branch (push_headers allocation)

claims.text: out-of-bounds read of heap memory adjacent to the header buffer, potentially disclosing sensitive data or causing a crash
claims.reasoning: The ASAN log in the report shows a heap-buffer-overflow in strlen called from curl_maprintf at lib/http2.c:1642. An out-of-bounds read can disclose adjacent heap memory (information disclosure) or hit unmapped memory (crash/DOS).

citations.note: curl_maprintf("%s:%s", name, value) will read past buffer end via strlen

claims.text: run an HTTP/2 server that pushes a stream with a header whose name and value are not null-terminated, then invoke curl with --http2-prior-knowledge against that server while ASAN is enabled
claims.reasoning: The reproduction steps are plausible: a malicious HTTP/2 server sends PUSH_PROMISE headers with non-null-terminated name/value buffers. The deterministic checks show the ungrounded symbols (H2Configuration, etc.) belong to the Python test script (h2 library), not curl itself, so they don't affect the curl code assessment.

key_reasons: lib/http2.c:1642 uses %s format specifiers on name/value pointers from nghttp2 without using the provided namelen/valuelen lengths
nghttp2 documentation explicitly states name/value pointers are NOT guaranteed to be null-terminated and applications MUST use length parameters
curl_maprintf processes %s by calling strlen, which reads past the buffer boundary when no null terminator exists
The fix is straightforward: use %.*s with the length parameters as already done correctly for trailers at line 1650-1651
This is reachable by a malicious HTTP/2 server sending PUSH_PROMISE headers, causing heap out-of-bounds read (information disclosure or crash)
reply: Thank you for the detailed report. The vulnerability is confirmed: lib/http2.c:1642 uses `%s:%s` with nghttp2 header pointers that are not guaranteed null-terminated, while the callback provides `namelen` and `valuelen`. The fix using `%.*s:%.*s` with the length parameters is correct and matches the pattern already used for trailers at line 1650. We will apply this fix.
